verifiedFindings: The Andalusian tourism authority identifies Sierra Morena as a Starlight Reserve and destination spanning the Sierra Norte de Sevilla natural park.

La Cartuja de Cazalla's current operator page offers advance-reserved guided telescope sessions and self-observation for booked accommodation guests; guided monitoring requires at least 15 days' notice and availability, while self-observers must book at least two nights.

The mapped La Cartuja monastery property supplies a reproducible property coordinate, but the exact observing area remains assigned by the host and the catalogue does not infer access from that map footprint.

The Astronomical Association of Spain publishes the exact El Castillo de las Guardas Observatory coordinate and an ongoing reservation procedure for public observations on suitable moonless Saturdays, subject to clear weather and minimum attendance.

The association's dated 2026 public calendar ended in September, so the revised record requires a newly confirmed session and operator-issued parking and walking instructions rather than representing the observatory as walk-in or independently accessible.

The association directs visitors to park in Peroamigo and walk under its instructions, warns that no services are nearby and publishes rural-footwear, warm-clothing, red-light, weather and fire-safety requirements.

The production Copernicus GLO-30 snapshots measure 575.070 metres at the La Cartuja property point and 465.631 metres at the operator-published observatory point; the catalogue records the reproducible rounded values of 575 and 466 metres.
The Cáceres provincial biosphere-reserve tourism authority explicitly identifies both Castillo de Monfragüe and Salto del Gitano as places for astronomical observation.
The authority's castle page describes designated parking followed by an approximately 20-minute walk and stairs; its route link locates the castle at 39.8281476, -6.0514947.
The authority's Salto del Gitano page describes access by car, motorcycle, bicycle or a signed walk from Villarreal de San Carlos; its route link locates the viewpoint at 39.8285483, -6.0578331.
The national-park visitor rules require use of designated viewpoint parking, prohibit camping and limit caravan or motorhome parking between 22:00 and 06:00 to no more than two consecutive hours.

The national-park itinerary page confirms Castillo de Monfragüe as a signed self-guided route and Salto del Gitano as a principal park viewpoint; current notices still take precedence over the prepared itinerary.

The Ávila provincial tourism authority identifies Navarredonda de Gredos and Hoyos del Espino as members of its purpose-built stellar-viewpoint network, whose facilities include a stable observing platform, parking, fencing, accessibility features and signed access.

The Navarredonda municipality documents a 23:00 astronomy event at Mirador Estelar de Navarredonda de Gredos, confirming night use of the named facility; the mapped viewpoint supplies the corrected coordinate 40.36303, -5.12396.

The Hoyos del Espino municipality documents a 22:30 astronomy event at Mirador Estelar Mesegosillo (Las Cocinillas), confirming night use of the named facility; the mapped viewpoint supplies the corrected coordinate 40.35239, -5.16424.
The Ávila Provincial Council states that the Sierra de Gredos Regional Park's Starlight Reserve certification was renewed in January 2025 for another four years.
The official sources support the named astronomy facilities but do not grant camping or override current local signs, temporary restrictions or mountain-weather decisions.
Galáctica's official visitor page documents bookable nighttime observations with professional telescopes, onsite parking, cold-weather advice and a weather-dependent cancellation process.
Galáctica's current activity calendar lists dated evening astronomy sessions, so the centre is represented as a booking-only programme venue rather than an independently accessible night site.
The official directions link identifies Galáctica at 39.9991162, -1.0407695, replacing the generic Arcos de las Salinas map point.
CEFCA locates the Observatorio Astrofísico de Javalambre at 40.0412972, -1.0164167 and 1,957 metres, while warning that its tracks require careful access planning and recommending a 4x4 vehicle.

The OAJ and Galáctica visitor pages route public OAJ visits through Galáctica and explicitly describe the OAJ visit as outreach rather than direct observing; it is therefore not presented as an independent night-observing stop.
Neither a Galáctica booking nor the regional Starlight context grants camping, after-hours access or permission to approach the research observatory outside the booked visitor arrangement.

The official Vall de Boí destination page identifies the national park and surrounding valley as a Starlight destination and explicitly names astronomical viewpoints at Boí Taüll and Sant Quirc de Durro.

The Boí Taüll Starlight viewpoint is located on the accessible walkway from car park P2, includes a planisphere for independent night-sky interpretation and hosts observing sessions on selected dates; the official station map confirms the parking, accessible route and Starlight facility layout.

The mapped P2 parking arrival area is 42.4793803, 0.8666296. It is used as the navigable coordinate because the official destination describes the viewpoint as reached from that car park rather than publishing a separate point coordinate.

The official Sant Quirc viewpoint page embeds the coordinate 42.4951864, 0.8111783 and states that independent visitors must walk about 20 minutes from the parking area at Durro's entrance; taxi access may be arranged.

The national-park authority states that private vehicles must remain at authorized entrance parking and that access inside the park continues on foot or by 4x4 taxi. Estany de Sant Maurici therefore cannot be presented as an independent drive-up observing stop.

Boí replaces Espot as the guide base because both verified astronomical viewpoints are in Vall de Boí; current signs, station operations, mountain weather and the published return route still determine whether either night visit proceeds.

The Vercors park authority and DarkSky International confirm that the southern three-quarters of the park form a 1,600-square-kilometre International Dark Sky Reserve designated in 2023, with a 245-square-kilometre core zone.
The Trièves tourism office identifies the public astronomy observatory at Résidence Les Dolomites, publishes the exact coordinate 44.90013, 5.554026 and gives precise visitor entrance directions.

The observatory's current listing publishes telescope-observing sessions for July, August and December 2026 and February, July and August 2027; the site is therefore represented as programme-only, not as independently open at night.

The official Gresse-en-Vercors visitor map marks both the astronomy observatory and nearby visitor parking, corroborating the named visitor setting without turning the coordinate into permission for after-hours access or camping.

Vercors Drôme Tourisme documents the 2026 Nuit des étoiles at Moulins de la Mure, including the exact coordinate 44.914771, 5.379652, evening sky interpretation and a weather fallback. The dated event does not establish routine access, so the venue is usable only when a new programme is published.

The generic Col de la Machine and Vassieux plateau pins lacked source support as specific astronomy visitor sites and are replaced by these two documented programme venues; Gresse-en-Vercors becomes the return base for the primary observatory plan.

The Sternenpark authority explicitly identifies Tauchplatz Dixi and Taferlklaussee among six designated Sternderl-schau’n visitor places and directs visitors to named public or hiking car parks, established paths and leave-no-trace conduct.
The Attersee-Attergau tourism authority confirms the Sternenpark's International Dark Sky recognition since 2021 and repeats both named observing places in its visitor guidance.

The official Dixi visitor listing identifies the site at B152 kilometre 10.6 in Weyregg, lists year-round operation, 20 parking spaces and a WC; the official tourism PDF publishes a coordinate within about 100 metres of the independent dive-coordinate reference 47.864608, 13.563412.

The official Taferlklaussee route describes the small car park directly at the lake, a larger nearby parking option and an elevation range of 772 to 786 metres; the published event meeting point locates the Taferlklausstube parking area at 47.843838, 13.626818.

The Sternenpark visitor rules require designated parking and marked paths and prohibit wild camping and fires. Both sites therefore remain limited-access shared visitor places rather than unrestricted night or camping locations.
Weyregg replaces Unterach as the return base because it is the municipality of the primary Dixi site and the official destination page publishes the town coordinate 47.90, 13.57.
The Großmugl municipality identifies a signed 1.5-kilometre Star Walk from Hauptstraße 46 to the Sternenrast at Leeberg and describes the route's nine astronomy interpretation stations.

Project Nightflight's current visitor guide states that the trail is available day and night, open year-round, free and without booking, with use of the mostly unlit field paths at the visitor's own risk; it recommends firm footwear, warm clothing and red light.

The visitor guide publishes the trailhead coordinate 48°29'39.8"N, 16°14'01.8"E, converted to 48.494389, 16.233833, and gives a roughly 20-minute walk each way between the village and the Sternenwiese.

The Sternenwiese and Sternenrast at Leeberg are explicitly described as the public observing endpoint of the trail. The Kuffner Observatory association publishes the Leeberg observing coordinate 48.500, 16.233 and confirms the community maintains observing fields at Leeberg and the Glühwürmchenwiese.
Museumsmanagement Niederösterreich lists the Star Walk as publicly operated, freely accessible at any time, with parking at the Hauptstraße 46 starting point.
The Kuffner Observatory association publishes dated 2026 guided star walks meeting at Station 1, Hauptstraße 46, and states that weather cancellations are announced 24 hours before the event.

The generic Leiser Berge map pin has no reviewed support as a specific visitor observing site and is removed; guided walks remain a separate programme record rather than permission to use an arbitrary field.
Runina municipality states that astronomical observing is possible directly in the village, that public lighting is switched off at 21:00 and that it is not switched on during summer.
The Poloniny National Park authority separately lists Runina among public night-sky observing locations and states that undisturbed observation is possible even from the village centre.

The village-centre coordinate 49.073369, 22.405239 identifies the public bus-stop and church area rather than an arbitrary meadow. The municipality and national-park trail information place Runina at about 550 metres elevation.

National-park visitor guidance requires marked routes, quiet conduct, designated camping and fire locations, so the village record does not imply access to adjoining private land, meadows or protected trails after dark.

Vihorlat Observatory publishes bookable evening observing programmes at the Astronomical Observatory on Kolonica Saddle, with a planetarium fallback when outdoor conditions prevent telescope observing; visits require a current reservation or published programme.

The observatory booking page publishes the venue coordinate 48°56′06.7″N, 22°16′26.4″E, converted to 48.935194, 22.273722. The colocated Slovak Hydrometeorological Institute station reports 431 metres elevation, which is used until the catalogue DEM pipeline refreshes the site.

Runina replaces Kolbasov as the return base because it is the independently usable primary observing location. The unsupported generic Runina meadow and Topľa valley pins are removed; Kolonica remains a separate programme-only alternative.

The Izera Dark-Sky Park register identifies the cross-border Izera and Jizerka valleys as an active dark-sky protection area founded by the University of Wrocław astronomy institute, Czech astronomy institute and the responsible Polish and Czech forest and landscape authorities.

The municipal visitor guides describe the signed route through Polana Izerska, Chatka Górzystów and Orle, but do not establish the generic meadow or Stóg Izerski pins as unrestricted night-observing sites.
The official Szklarska Poręba visitor page documents an astronomy day with night observing at Orle, the coordinate 50°48′54.5″N, 15°22′58.3″E and an elevation of 820 metres.

The same official event page states that Orle is reached from Jakuszyce on foot, by bicycle or by car only for overnight guests, and that the organised night walk runs only in suitable weather with a minimum group. The catalogue therefore requires a newly published programme plus a confirmed overnight or guided return plan.

The municipal Izerska Łąka education centre states that its two telescopes are used for night observing only on designated dates. Its rules prohibit unaffiliated visitors anywhere on the property outside operating hours.
Świeradów-Zdrój published a registration-required astronomy evening at Izerska Łąka on 12 August 2026, confirming the venue's event use without implying routine after-hours access.

The centre's official embedded map identifies 50.9278741, 15.314116 at Rolnicza 7. A live Open-Meteo elevation lookup returned 467 metres for that point; the catalogue DEM pipeline will independently replace or confirm it during the combined ingestion run.

The unsupported generic Izera Meadow and Stóg Izerski observation records are removed. Orle becomes the programme-only primary site and stay area; Izerska Łąka remains a separately confirmed event alternative.
Glamping Tara's operator directly promotes two reservable all-season panoramic domes in Rastište as accommodation beneath the stars and publishes telephone, messaging and email booking contacts.

The operator-linked map resolves the Glamping Tara guest property to 43.949661, 19.356679. Serbia.com's operator listing independently describes the stay as suited to sleeping and stargazing beneath Tara's stars and links visitors back to the booking provider.

Garden Hill Tara's operator offers four reservable villas at Konjska Reka 422 in Mitrovac and explicitly describes evening use of its private pool beneath the starry sky. The operator-linked map resolves the accommodation complex to 43.9210566, 19.4198053.

Both replacement records are accommodation-only guest footprints. A current overnight booking and the host's assigned outdoor area support use of the selected property; neither record grants access to a park viewpoint, trail, forest road, adjacent parcel or the other accommodation.

The current Tara National Park visitor rules require use of marked routes and arranged or designated places, prohibit camping outside designated locations and restrict vehicle movement on forest roads or outside designated routes unless specifically authorised. The guide therefore includes no after-dark transfer or park fallback.

Open-Meteo supplied preliminary elevation cross-checks of 439 metres for Glamping Tara and 1,106 metres for Garden Hill Tara. Production Copernicus DEM GLO-30 samples at the reviewed coordinates are 436.087 and 1092.862 metres; the catalogue stores the rounded values 436 and 1,093 metres.

HostGost directly offers Armadillo Houses as year-round private cabins with private terraces and an embedded operator map at 43.2767046, 20.7676804. Its current Kopaonik portfolio explicitly promotes falling asleep with a view of the starry sky, and its direct booking engine exposes current reservation enquiries.

The Armadillo catalogue point is limited to the checked-in guest terrace assigned by the host. Optical equipment requires direct host approval, and the stay does not grant access to neighbouring properties, ski infrastructure or National Park terrain.

Grand Kopaonik directly offers bookable hotel accommodation and describes a 22-by-8-metre heated outdoor pool as a pool under the stars. Its contact page publishes reservation, reception and spa contacts, including a separate spa telephone number.

The Grand catalogue point uses the OpenStreetMap hotel-building centroid at 43.2845315, 20.8114871 and is limited to quiet unaided sky viewing from a staff-managed guest or confirmed spa area. The pool is not represented as a telescope pad, and equipment is excluded unless the hotel separately approves and assigns a safe footprint.

Kopaonik National Park visitor rules and tourist map remain the outer boundary for both accommodation records. A room or cabin booking does not authorise Pančićev vrh, Sunčana dolina, a piste, lift, forest road or park trail after dark, so the route includes no night transfer or fallback.

Open-Meteo supplied preliminary elevation cross-checks of 1,376 metres for Armadillo Houses and 1,730 metres for Grand Kopaonik. Production Copernicus DEM GLO-30 samples at the reviewed coordinates are 1394.030 and 1731.441 metres; the catalogue stores the rounded values 1,394 and 1,731 metres.

The former summit and lower-lift-station candidates and the old Konaci stay record are removed. Both replacement accommodation sites remain inactive and their images remain pending license verification.

SANParks publishes exact GPS waypoints for Potjiespram Camp at S 28°04.482′, E 16°57.789′ and De Hoop at S 28°11.021′, E 17°10.682′. These convert to -28.0747, 16.96315 and -28.1836833, 17.1780333 and replace the materially incorrect staged coordinates.

The same official waypoint register places Sendelingsdrift at S 28°07.514′, E 16°53.496′, converted to -28.1252333, 16.8916. This replaces the coarse and incorrect stay-area coordinate while retaining Sendelingsdrift as the reception, permit and supply base.

SANParks describes Potjiespram as a bookable Orange River campsite near reception. The park management plan identifies Potjiespram and De Hoop as designated camping facilities, and the internal rules allow camping and overnight stays only in designated accommodation areas known to park management.

SANParks explicitly promotes stargazing as a Richtersveld experience. That supports observing from a booked campsite but does not create permission for a separate roadside, riverbank or desert viewpoint.

Official travel guidance requires admission and overnight permits at Sendelingsdrift, asks overnight visitors to arrive before 16:00, prohibits driving in the park at night and requires appropriate high-clearance or 4x4 capability. The guide and route therefore keep the vehicle at one booked camp throughout the dark interval.

Visitor guidance requires water, food, spares and night lighting, warns of extreme temperatures, heavy dew, scorpions and evening wind, and prohibits driving outside indicated routes and camping sites. The catalogue text incorporates these operational limits rather than treating darkness alone as readiness.

A reviewed Open-Meteo elevation lookup returned 42 metres for Potjiespram, 81 metres for De Hoop and 37 metres for Sendelingsdrift. The first two replace implausible staged elevations of 410 and 480 metres but remain subject to independent confirmation by the combined catalogue DEM ingestion.

Both observation records remain inactive and both image records remain pending. Factual verification clears only the source-content gate; real snapshots and verified image licences are still required before activation.

SANParks identifies Leokwe Rest Camp as Mapungubwe's main bookable camp in the eastern section and Mazhou Camp Site as a ten-pitch bookable campground in the western section. These replace the unsupported generic 'Mapungubwe camp area' record.

The mapped Leokwe facility is at -22.2177486, 29.3648104 and the mapped SANParks-operated Mazhou campsite is at -22.187385, 29.2012847. Open-Meteo returned preliminary elevations of 544 and 528 metres; production Copernicus DEM GLO-30 samples are 546.995 and 532.697 metres, and the catalogue stores 547 and 533 metres.
SANParks publishes the Main Gate coordinate as 22°14′37″S, 29°24′2″E, converted to -22.2436111, 29.4005556. The exact gate and reception record replaces the generic Mapungubwe stay-area coordinate.

SANParks locates the Confluence Viewpoint at 22°10′00″S, 29°10′00″E and describes it as a scenic heritage viewpoint and picnic area. It does not identify the viewpoint as an astronomy site or confirm independent use after dark, so the materially incorrect staged Confluence pin is removed rather than promoted as a night location.

Current SANParks visitor guidance states that unguided walking is prohibited because large and dangerous game occurs in the park, Leokwe is unfenced, other camps use only elephant-exclusion fencing and animals can move through and around camps. It also states that outdoor camp lighting is limited and guests require a torch or headlamp outside at night.

The national rules allow overnight guests only at booked recognised facilities, require reception before occupation and prohibit after-hours driving. Together with the camp-lighting guidance, this supports only brief unaided sky viewing immediately beside the occupied unit or pitch, with a torch ready and immediate indoor retreat; it does not support a walking route, telescope setup or separate viewpoint.

SANParks published a 19 May 2026 notice that renovation work at Leokwe and Mazhou could begin at any time and cause disruption. Any later use therefore requires a current booking and dated confirmation of construction status plus compliance with current camp instructions.

Access to Mazhou requires checking in at the Main Gate and driving outside the park to rejoin the western section. This rules out treating Leokwe and Mazhou as two stops in one night and reinforces that any confirmed plan must remain within one assigned accommodation footprint.

Both replacement site records remain inactive and both image records remain pending. Their access scores reflect a bookable but wildlife-constrained overnight footprint, not a public astronomy venue, and no activation is permitted while image licences remain unresolved.
Sark's official visitor service confirms contact-based booking for the island observatory and says the Sark Astronomy Society offers year-round telescope sessions at the Dachinger Observatory.
The same official service identifies La Valette as a permitted bookable campsite and explicitly promotes nighttime constellation viewing from its grass.

The revised records use the exact observatory and campsite footprints, distinguish the guided programme from a campsite booking and do not present the lighthouse lookout, coastal paths or private land as observing overflow.

Eselbe Camp's current official pages identify a bookable Nata River eco-camp, offer self-camping and other overnight accommodation, publish reservation and access directions and explicitly promote evening stargazing by the communal fireside.

Gaing-O Community Trust identifies itself as custodian and campsite operator at Kubu Island. Its current rules require registration, designated campsites, marked-road driving, designated fireplaces, quiet use and proof of payment.
The Trust's visually verified 2025-2027 price list charges per-night camping and separately lists stargazing; it also states that camping outside gazetted areas is prohibited by law.
The revised records use the mapped Eselbe Camp footprint and a mapped designated Kubu camp pitch. The old generic Nata Sanctuary pin and materially incorrect Kubu approach coordinate are removed.

The two records are separate overnight bookings and never a two-stop night route. Eselbe observing remains in the host-managed fireside footprint; Kubu observing remains in the assigned campsite after a daylight arrival and current road-opening check.

Open-Meteo returned preliminary elevations of 912 metres at Eselbe and 903 metres at Kubu. Production Copernicus DEM GLO-30 samples are 911.142 and 908.568 metres, and the catalogue stores 911 and 909 metres.

Tsumkwe Country Lodge publishes a direct booking path, ten campsites, official GPS coordinates, daily reception hours and a walled and fenced guest boundary. It warns that elephants and antelope frequently visit the waterhole and provides night security for late arrivals.

The Ju/'Hoansi Living Museum publishes its exact Grashoek location, operation until sundown, reception-based campsite acceptance and manager contact. Its FAQ requires cash payment with a receipt, says campsite pre-booking is neither necessary nor possible and requires a 4x4 for overnight campsite access.

The visually verified 2026-2027 Ju/'Hoansi programme lists three campsites with a dry toilet, bucket shower and braai, plus separately paid guided evening storytelling and cultural activities. Camping does not imply unguided museum, village or bush access after dark.

Neither selected operator advertises an independent astronomy field. Both records therefore default to brief unaided or handheld-binocular viewing beside the occupied guest or campsite footprint; optical equipment requires explicit operator approval and no after-dark transfer is included.

The former Living Hunter's Museum at /Xa//oba closed in January 2026. LCFN describes its possible replacement as a development project, so neither the closed site nor the proposed site is a visitor fallback.

The revised records replace the generic Tsumkwe community-area and Naye-Naye pins with the official lodge GPS and the mapped Grashoek campground. Open-Meteo returned preliminary elevations of 1,150 and 1,203 metres; the production Copernicus pipeline must replace or confirm them.
The reviewed destination and conservation sources establish Rakiura/Stewart Island as a dark-sky destination with sensitive coastal and national-park environments.
They do not establish the coarse Oban shoreline and Horseshoe Bay pins as approved independent observing footprints or document the intended after-dark return.

requiredChanges.reason: Obtain current local or DOC confirmation for two named public night-viewing places, including exact parking, pedestrian route, wildlife precautions and closing rules, or replace the staged pins.

verifiedFindings: Parks SA explicitly promotes Flinders Chase for stargazing and documents Rocky River and West Bay as separate bookable campgrounds.

The revised coordinates are representative points inside the official georeferenced campground footprints; West Bay requires 4WD and may close after rain, while Rocky River has allocated sites and visitor facilities.
The revised guide requires one booked campsite for the complete night, daylight arrival and departure, and no attraction-to-attraction or campground-to-campground driving after dark.

Mudgee Region Tourism and the operator confirm that Mudgee Observatory at 961 Old Grattai Road runs public day and night sessions by essential advance booking; seasonal session times are supplied with the booking.
The operator's published coordinate and the mapped observatory feature resolve the exact visitor facility, replacing the former coarse regional pin.

The unsupported Gulgong record is replaced by Grattai Grove: its official destination listing publishes the exact property coordinate and explicitly promotes Milky Way stargazing after nightfall, while the operator confirms two bookable accommodation options, onsite parking directions and wildlife risk on twilight and night approaches.

The revised route is programme-only: visitors use either one confirmed observatory session or a separately booked Grattai Grove accommodation footprint, never both on one night and never a roadside or paddock substitute.
Western Australia's park service identifies Boorabbin National Park as a visitor stop on the Great Eastern Highway.
No reviewed authority source identifies the staged woodland and Holland Track coordinates as astronomy sites, and remote-road darkness does not establish safe parking or overnight permission.

requiredChanges.reason: Replace both generic pins with named DBCA campgrounds or day-use facilities and obtain explicit night-use, fire, road and closure rules before creating an observing route.

verifiedFindings: Ontario identifies the Highland Pond parking area off Southwood Road as the reserve's formal main access, and the exact unpaved parking polygon is mapped at 44.9415459, -79.5135668.

The Guardians identify the smooth granite outcrop immediately behind the Ministry sign as the main dark-sky viewing area; a geotagged 2024 nighttime photograph documents a separate footprint at 44.942622, -79.513414 north of the parking and beside the first trail segment.

The current trail page marks Pine Ridge Loop temporarily closed and its eastern connecting boardwalk out of operation, so the route remains at the main viewing outcrop and does not promote the ridge alternative.

Current reserve rules permit camping and fire-making only at six designated campsites away from the viewing area; neither the parking record nor the viewing record grants camping or fire permission, and same-day Ontario Parks alerts remain a required check.

The completed Copernicus DEM ingestion measured 245.773 metres at the granite viewing point and 247.952 metres at the parking point; the catalogue stores the corresponding rounded elevations of 246 and 248 metres.
Both catalogue records remain inactive, and both image licences remain pending.
Parks Canada recommends Chignecto Campground as the base close to Fundy's stargazing activity and Wolfe Lake as a secluded viewing place.
Parks Canada publishes the Chignecto Campground coordinate and a Wolfe Lake visitor coordinate, allowing the two staged records to use named visitor footprints rather than coarse park-area pins.
The revised records preserve campground booking and season checks, current opening and road checks, daylight arrival, established visitor surfaces and a return to the booked overnight base.

The operator's Night Pass links the named DarkSky Observation Field at 45.6694987, -81.9708103 and a separate DarkSky parking lot, grants checked-in access from sunset to sunrise, and publishes the Saturday-event and hunting-period exclusions.

The current Astro Night / Aurora Hunting programme begins with registration outside the Nature Center at the operator-published venue address, then uses an operator-led convoy from the main parking lot to DarkSky Parking and a guided session at the same observation field.

The gate closes to vehicles at sunset; Night Pass visitors park outside it and carry equipment for the published 6–12 minute walk. Forest Campgrounds are off-limits to pass visitors, and white light, personal laser pointers and campfires are prohibited in the preserve.
RASC confirms the designated preserve, large 360-degree observation field, public astronomy programming and after-dark vehicle boundary.

The completed Copernicus DEM ingestion measured 239.721 metres at the observation field and 233.225 metres at the programme check-in; the catalogue stores the corresponding rounded elevations of 240 and 233 metres.
The generic Meldrum Bay and Sheguiandah pins have been removed. Both replacement records remain inactive, and both image licences remain pending.

BLM explicitly promotes stargazing and permits dispersed camping throughout Massacre Rim Dark Sky Sanctuary; Massacre Ranch and Steven's Camp are named public recreation areas with primitive campsites and first-come cabins.

The official California National Historic Trail brochure supplies exact interpretive-panel coordinates at Massacre Ranch and Steven's Camp, replacing the coarse sanctuary point and the invalid Denio observing record.

BLM documents gravel Nevada 8A near the sanctuary, extremely rough and rocky interior roads, a four-wheel-drive/high-clearance recommendation, no cell service, unreliable surface water and fuel approximately 40 to 90 road miles away.

The current Winnemucca fire order prohibits wood and charcoal fires outside developed fee campgrounds or picnic areas, with a narrow portable gas or pressurised-liquid stove exception, and the High Rock Canyon Road southern approach has a recurring winter/spring closure.
Copernicus DEM GLO-30 samples at the reviewed coordinates are 1817.051 metres for Massacre Ranch and 1755.659 metres for Steven's Camp; the catalogue stores the rounded values 1817 and 1756 metres.

NPS explicitly supports self-directed night stargazing in Parashant, requires daylight hazard scouting and designated parking, and warns that the monument has no towns, services, gasoline or dependable cell coverage.

The official BLM national recreation-site layer maps Mount Trumbull Trailhead at 36.39191793, -113.15106744 and the Poverty Junction toilet at 36.39449207, -113.57941422; NPS independently documents the associated CR5 trailhead and CR103/BLM1046 vault-toilet parking contexts.

Mount Trumbull Trailhead is a named BLM stargazing visitor site with parking and a vault toilet. Poverty Junction is retained only as a separate one-stop parking option; neither record is represented as a campsite, and Tuweep is removed because it lies in Grand Canyon National Park under separate rules.

NPS requires high-clearance four-wheel drive and all-terrain tyres for these routes, states that CR5 around Mount Trumbull is usually impassable from December through February, and warns that the CR103 clay roadbed can remain impassable for days after heavy rain.

All drinking water, fuel margin, recovery equipment, offline navigation and independent communications must be carried. The possible summer spigot at Mount Trumbull is untreated and unreliable, while current road, smoke, weather, closure and Arizona fire information must be rechecked for every trip.

Open-Meteo supplied preliminary elevation cross-checks of 1,983 metres for Mount Trumbull Trailhead and 1,769 metres for Poverty Junction. Copernicus DEM GLO-30 samples at the reviewed coordinates are 1983.139 and 1770.476 metres; the catalogue stores the rounded values 1,983 and 1,770 metres.

Arizona State Parks explicitly defines two night-sky access models: public Star Parties near Kannally Ranch House on published dates and independently reservable after-hours entry at the American Avenue side gate.
Independent visitors must call before 15:00, preferably on the same day, pay the current fee and obtain a four-digit padlock code; overnight camping remains prohibited.

The American Avenue record uses the mapped parking point inside the official trailhead footprint. The Kannally Ranch House record uses the exact mapped building and remains unavailable unless the park publishes a new dated astronomy event or supplies a written arrangement.
The current Oracle event calendar reviewed on 2026-09-22 lists no future astronomy event, so the Ranch House site has publicAccess no and accessScore 0 rather than implying routine night entry.

The completed Copernicus DEM ingestion measured 1307.162 metres at American Avenue and 1325.952 metres at Kannally Ranch House; the catalogue stores the corresponding rounded elevations of 1307 and 1326 metres.
The unsupported Charouleau Gap record and the old coarse Ranch House pin have been removed. Both replacements and their images remain inactive and pending.
Texas Parks and Wildlife explicitly promotes stargazing, camping and star parties at Enchanted Rock and publishes daily park and gate hours.

The revised day-use record uses the official D2 footprint at the south Loop Trail trailhead; all trails except the Loop Trail close shortly after sunset, so the summit is no longer recommended at night.
The revised overnight record uses the official walk-in tent-site area and preserves booking, late-arrival gate-code, trail-closure, quiet and lighting rules.
Virginia DCR identifies Staunton River as an International Dark Sky Park and states that the field next to the visitor center is available year-round for astronomical observation.
The park publishes guided summer sessions and registered spring and autumn star parties while keeping independent field use subject to parking fees and current park information.
The staged observing-field and campground records remain inactive until their real climate, darkness and DEM snapshots and image licences are complete.
Florida State Parks documents a reservable astronomy pad with red-light and no-fire rules, and the official accommodation GIS identifies Astronomy Pad A exactly.
The revised fallback record uses the official pavilion beside the entrance kiosk, where visitors without a reservation or eligible after-hours permit are directed to observe.
The revised access notes distinguish both footprints and preserve reservation, ranger contact, arrival-before-sunset, red-light, bathroom and gate rules.
NPS promotes year-round stargazing and publishes current ranger programmes at the south end of Seagrape Drive; an official NPS event record maps that programme footprint exactly.
NPS separately publishes an exact coordinate and year-round visitor information for Midway Campground, while Recreation.gov supplies its reservation and quiet-hour rules.
